griesel-blanc-de-noirs.producerStory: Griesel & Compagnie was founded in 2013 in Bensheim as the first dedicated sparkling-wine house on Germany's tiny Hessische Bergstraße, working out of a historic 1904 estate with a vaulted cellar. Cellar master Niko Brandner — a former banker who retrained in viticulture — quickly pushed Griesel into the top tier of German Sekt, making traditional-method (bottle-fermented) wines with a minimum of about 20 months on the lees. The Blanc de Noirs is white sparkling pressed from the red Champagne grapes Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier.
griesel-blanc-de-noirs.whyWePourIt: It's the serious grower-Champagne experience at a friendlier price — the bottle for guests who want real traditional-method bubbles with a story they haven't heard before.

gulfi-nerojbleo.producerStory: Gulfi is a family estate just north of Chiaramonte Gulfi in southeastern Sicily, founded by Vito Catania and now run by his son Matteo, farming around 70 hectares of native Sicilian varieties organically. They were pioneers of single-vineyard Nero d'Avola, and Nerojbleo is their benchmark bottling — 100% Nero d'Avola from older vines on the hilly, calcareous-marl sites of the Hyblaean hills, aged about 12 months in barrique. The higher-elevation fruit gives a fresher, more structured take on Sicily's signature dark grape.
gulfi-nerojbleo.whyWePourIt: It fills the big-Sicilian-red slot with grip and savour instead of jam — the structured warm-climate Italian that flatters lamb and ribeye without tasting like a fruit bomb.

kistler.producerStory: Kistler Vineyards was founded in 1978 by Steve Kistler and Mark Bixler in Sonoma County, and built its cult reputation on single-vineyard, single-clone Chardonnay before adding Pinot Noir from the same exacting playbook. Based in the Russian River Valley since 1992, the winery works a handful of cool Sonoma sites, with its Pinot program built on heritage vine selections of Burgundian origin. Winemaker Jason Kesner has led the cellar since Steve Kistler's 2017 retirement, keeping the house style plush, precise and site-driven.
kistler.whyWePourIt: This is the splurge Pinot — a California cult name guests recognize, giving the list a true special-occasion light red between Burgundy and the steak Cabs.

landron-muscadet-sevre-et-maine-amphibol.producerStory: Jo Landron took over his family's domaine near Nantes in 1990 and grew it to about 50 hectares of Melon de Bourgogne, converting to certified organic farming in 2002 and certified biodynamics in 2011 — he's one of Muscadet's reference growers. Amphibolite is named for the greenish metamorphic sea-floor rock under this single 7.5-hectare parcel; it's hand-harvested, fermented with natural yeasts and aged briefly on fine lees in concrete to stay lean, citrusy and saline. It's made to be drunk young, as the purest expression of that rock.
landron-muscadet-sevre-et-maine-amphibol.whyWePourIt: Every raw-bar list needs the textbook oyster wine, and this is it — bone-dry, salty, organic Muscadet from a benchmark grower at a gentle price.

malahierba-vinos-maleza.producerStory: Malahierba is a tiny project started in the late 2010s (first vintage 2019) by agricultural engineers Silvia Rocher and Manuel García in the Sierra de Salamanca, the wild mountain country of western Spain near Portugal. They rescue heritage parcels of the local Rufete grape — many vines 80 to 120 years old, never treated with herbicides — working only about 5 hectares in total. Maleza is a single high-altitude granite parcel near San Esteban de la Sierra, gently extracted and aged in acacia, with production measured in hundreds of bottles in some vintages.
malahierba-vinos-maleza.whyWePourIt: It's the insider's light red — a rare old-vine mountain grape with Pinot-like brightness that gives the Burgundy-curious guest a genuine discovery.

maloof-where-ya-pjs-at.producerStory: Maloof Wines is run by Ross and Bee Maloof — he came out of a decade in Philadelphia restaurants, she from aerospace materials engineering — at their vineyard and winery near Forest Grove in the northwest Willamette Valley, certified organic since 2020. They specialize in aromatic grapes underrepresented in Oregon, especially Pinot Gris and Riesling. Where Ya PJs At? is their playful orange wine: Pinot Gris fermented dry on its skins (around three weeks), blended with barrel-fermented Riesling, and bottled unfined and unfiltered.
maloof-where-ya-pjs-at.whyWePourIt: It's the list's orange-wine moment — savory, grippy and fun, bridging white and red for charcuterie and grilled plates while signalling we take natural wine seriously without being precious about it.

mount-eden-wolff-vineyard.producerStory: Mount Eden Vineyards is a historic Santa Cruz Mountains estate whose winemaking has been guided by Jeffrey Patterson since 1981, with a Burgundian, low-intervention approach. For this bottling they've sourced Chardonnay from the same Edna Valley planting since 1985 — vines planted in 1976 by local pioneer Andy MacGregor, in a vineyard owned by Jean Pierre Wolff since 1999. Cool Pacific air makes Edna Valley one of California's chilliest growing regions, so the wine keeps bright acid and stony freshness under its barrel-fermented texture.
mount-eden-wolff-vineyard.whyWePourIt: It's the serious crossover Chardonnay — California richness with white-Burgundy poise from a legacy producer, perfect for the guest who 'doesn't do buttery Chard.'

pierre-thibert-chorey-les-beaune.producerStory: Pierre Thibert wasn't born into wine — he built his small family domaine in Corgoloin from scratch in 1989, and with his wife Aline now farms roughly ten acres of vines including Chorey-lès-Beaune, Nuits-Saint-Georges and Côte de Nuits villages. The work is traditional and detail-obsessed, with maturation in tank or used wood depending on the cuvée, and the domaine has a loyal French following with regular citations in guides like the Guide Hachette. His Chorey-lès-Beaune is honest, earthy village Burgundy from the flats below Aloxe-Corton.
pierre-thibert-chorey-les-beaune.whyWePourIt: It's the friendly door into real red Burgundy — an artisan grower's Pinot that delivers the forest-floor experience without a Grand Cru markup.

raventos-i-blanc-de-nit-rose.producerStory: The Raventós family has grown vines on this Penedès estate since 1497, and ancestor Josep Raventós made Spain's first traditional-method sparkling wine in 1872 — effectively inventing Cava. In 2012 Raventós i Blanc famously walked away from the Cava DO to create the stricter Conca del Riu Anoia designation: estate fruit, native grapes, biodynamic farming and longer aging. De Nit is their pale rosé — the classic trio of Xarel·lo, Macabeu and Parellada tinted with a small dose of Monastrell, aged around 18 months on the lees.
raventos-i-blanc-de-nit-rose.whyWePourIt: It's the sparkling rosé with pedigree — bone-dry, saline and food-first from the family that invented Cava and then outgrew it, ideal for oysters and crudo.

sandrine-fabrice-gasnier-chinon-pierres-.producerStory: Fabrice Gasnier is a fourth-generation grower in Cravant-les-Côteaux, the heart of Chinon, where he and his wife Sandrine farm around thirty hectares of mostly old-vine Cabernet Franc. The domaine has been biodynamic since 2008, certified by both Ecocert and Demeter. Les Pierres Chaudes ('warm stones') comes from clay-silica soils strewn with small stones over limestone — a sunny site that gives riper, rounder fruit while keeping Chinon's signature peppery, herbal edge.
sandrine-fabrice-gasnier-chinon-pierres-.whyWePourIt: It's the sommelier's mid-weight red — biodynamic Loire Cab Franc whose leafy, peppery savour flatters herbs, charcuterie and lamb in a way crowd-pleaser reds can't.

terroir-sense-fronteres-negre-de-montsan.producerStory: Terroir Sense Fronteres ('terroir without borders') is Dominik Huber's Montsant project, launched in 2016 as a sister to Terroir al Límit, the Priorat estate he co-founded with Eben Sadie in 2001 and has run solo since 2012. The approach is radically hands-off: organic farming, hand harvest, whole-bunch fermentation with wild yeasts, no oak — Negre is Garnatxa from vines around Capçanes at 300–350 metres, raised entirely in stainless steel. The result is Montsant with Priorat-adjacent minerality but fresher, lighter hands.
terroir-sense-fronteres-negre-de-montsan.whyWePourIt: It's the fresh, stony Grenache that proves warm-climate Spain can be lifted and savory — the natural step up for anyone who loves our by-the-glass Garnacha.

texier-brezeme.producerStory: Éric Texier is a former nuclear engineer from Bordeaux who retrained in wine (including time with Jean-Marie Guffens in Burgundy) and became famous for resurrecting forgotten Rhône terroirs. His signature rescue is Brézème, a lone south-facing hill at the very southern tip of the northern Rhône that had 19th-century fame alongside Hermitage before nearly vanishing; Texier replanted and now farms most of his own vines there. His style is self-described old-school and minimalist — cool, peppery, savory Syrah rather than a jammy bruiser.
texier-brezeme.whyWePourIt: It's the savory Syrah slot — black pepper, olive and smoke with real freshness for the lamb and steak crowd, plus a great comeback story servers can actually tell.

white-rock.producerStory: White Rock is one of Napa's 'ghost wineries' — established in 1870 by Dr. John Pettingill, who built the winery from white volcanic stone quarried on the property in the southern foothills of the Stags Leap range. Henri and Claire Vandendriessche bought and revived the estate in 1977, and their family still farms it, producing only around 3,000 cases a year of estate Cabernet Sauvignon, Claret and Chardonnay. The house style is classic and age-worthy rather than over-ripe — old-school Napa from volcanic-ash soils.
white-rock.whyWePourIt: It's the top steak Cabernet on the list — a small family estate with 150 years of history, giving big-night guests structure and a story instead of just a famous label.

whitehall-lane.producerStory: Whitehall Lane Winery sits on a St. Helena site first planted to vines in the 1800s; the modern winery was founded in 1979 and bought in 1993 by the Leonardini family of San Francisco, who still run it today. The family built its reputation on Merlot and Cabernet, farming eight estate vineyards totalling more than 200 acres across St. Helena, Rutherford, Oak Knoll and beyond. Their Merlot is a long-running Napa benchmark for the plush, polished style.
whitehall-lane.whyWePourIt: It's the smooth crowd-pleaser among the structured reds — a family-grown Napa Merlot soft enough to flatter almost any table when a big Cab would be too much.
